thread.title: ASIA MARKETS: Asian Markets Tumble, Following Tech Losses On Wall Street

author: morningstar.com
title: ASIA MARKETS: Asian Markets Tumble, Following Tech Losses On Wall Street
text:
By Dow Jones Newswires
Nikkei down more than 3%; Apple component suppliers hit hard
Asian stock markets plunged in early trading Tuesday following Monday's rout, led by tech stocks, on Wall Street.
Every sector in Japan's stock market turned lower as the Nikkei dropped more than 3%. Investors were quick to react to the U.S. losses, especially among suppliers linked to Apple's (AAPL) iPhone. TDK (6762.TO) and Murata (6981.TO) were down about 8% and 4%, respectively. Meanwhile, SoftBank (9984.TO) rose slightly, making up an early 4% loss, following its after-the-bell update on the planned IPO for its Japanese mobile unit. Japanese auto companies also fell after reports that the Trump administration is planning tariffs on auto imports, with Toyota (7203.TO) and Honda (HMC) down about 3% each.
Hong Kong stocks joined the selloff, as the Hang Seng Index fell 1.5%. Index heavyweight Tencent (0700.HK) slid another 2% while smartphone-component maker AAC (2018.HK) skidded nearly 3.6% more. Energy stocks were also weak with oil's sharp reversal, with oil giant CNOOC (0883.HK) falling 4%.
Mainland China stocks fared better, with the Shanghai Composite down 0.5% and the smaller-cap Shenzhen Composite about flat. IPhone component suppliers Secote Precision (603283.SH) and Luxshare (002475.SZ) were down some 3.5% and 6.5%, respectively.
Benchmark indexes in South Korea and Taiwan dropped more than 1%, weighed down by tech names. Samsung (005930.SE) fell almost 3% and SK Hynix (000660.SE) plummeted 5% while Taiwan Semiconductor (2330.TW) was off 2%.
Australia's ASX 200 was down almost 2%, as energy and financial names dropped, and New Zealand stocks slipped about 1%.
